-38.50898,-13.00493.name: CENAFERT - Centro de Medicina Reprodutiva
-38.50898,-13.00493.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.cenafert.com.br. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-90.34100,38.65100.name: Benson Hill
-90.34100,38.65100.state: St Louis — 1001 N Warson Rd, BRDG Park
-90.34100,38.65100.desc: Used computational breeding and editing to design soy for protein content, raised heavily on that promise, and went bankrupt in 2025. The technology worked well enough, and the company still could not build a business between the four majors and the commodity buyers. It is the clearest recent evidence that the concentration on this map is not only about patents — the distribution and processing chain is closed too.

-71.05300,42.35400.name: Blackstone Life Sciences
-71.05300,42.35400.desc: The life sciences arm of one of the world’s largest private equity firms, funding late-stage drug development. Capital of this size chooses which candidates reach patients, applying a return requirement at the point where clinical need would otherwise decide.

-71.08700,42.36000.name: Colossal — Breaking spin-out and IP licensing
-71.08700,42.36000.desc: A spin-out applying the de-extinction company's enzyme engineering to plastic degradation. It is the pattern worth noting rather than the product: a venture raised on returning extinct animals generates conventional industrial biotechnology as a by-product, and the by-product is what has a market.

11.97000,57.69000.name: Vitrolife
11.97000,57.69000.desc: Supplies much of the culture media, equipment and consumables that IVF laboratories worldwide depend on. An embryo develops in this company’s media, and the 2024 recall by a competitor showed what a supplier failure destroys — something irreplaceable, in a market regulated as devices rather than as the environment an embryo grows in.

6.13000,46.18000.name: Firmenich / flavour and fragrance biotechnology
6.13000,46.18000.desc: Flavour compounds once extracted from plants are increasingly brewed by engineered microbes instead — vanillin being the clearest case. That displaces the farmers who grew the plant, in countries with no say in the decision, and the substitution happens inside a supply chain rather than through any policy anyone can object to.

-58.70000,-34.51000.name: Sinergium Biotech
-58.70000,-34.51000.desc: The private Argentine biopharmaceutical company that is the other Latin American partner in the mRNA transfer programme, working at pilot scale on the platform developed in Cape Town. It sits in the same industrial corridor north of Buenos Aires as the country's veterinary vaccine manufacturing, which is worth noticing: human and animal recombinant production, the first engineered wheat and the regulator that wrote the gene-editing criteria others copied are all within a short distance of each other, and this map has generally recorded them as though they were separate industries.

127.43000,36.72000.name: Biotoxtech
127.43000,36.72000.state: Ochang, Cheongju, North Chungcheong — with subsidiaries
127.43000,36.72000.desc: A Korean contract research organisation running non-clinical safety studies for pharmaceuticals, food, cosmetics, cell therapies, chemicals and agrochemicals from a facility of around 146,000 square feet, and it states it is the only domestic private CRO to hold good laboratory practice accreditation from the US food and drug administration, alongside full international laboratory animal care accreditation. Its group divides the work across subsidiaries: one for non-clinical pharmacology and bioanalysis including PCR-based biodistribution for cell and gene therapies, and another offering primate-based toxicology and efficacy studies and inhalation toxicology. Biodistribution studies for gene therapies are how a regulator learns where an engineered vector travels in a body, and that work sits here.
